Q1: L-Glutamic acid presents known dermal and eye hazards (Tier 1), along with an expanded perspective on carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards (Tier 2). It also has demonstrated low to moderate oral hazards (Tier 3). However, there is insufficient data to confidently assess its environmental, endocrine disruption, inhalation, and organ/systemic hazards (Tier 4).
Q2: L-Glutamic acid is generally considered of low concern, appearing on the EPA's "Substances Added to Food" inventory and FDA's "Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS)" list.
Q3: This chemical is extensively characterized in the scientific literature, with over 200,000 references, and has a precisely defined molecular structure. Although it has some toxicological data available, it has not undergone comprehensive EPA evaluations, and significant data gaps remain in several hazard categories.
